question: What shape is the anterior fontanelle (the soft spot towards the front of a baby's head)?

options.A: Triangle
options.B: Square
options.C: Circle
options.D: Diamond

explanation: The anterior fontanelle is famously diamond-shaped. This is a classic midwife clue that helps you tell it apart from the triangular posterior fontanelle during an exam!

question: Which of these is NOT a main goal for a community nurse working to prevent disease?

options.A: Promoting local participation in mass immunization campaigns
options.B: Enforcing mandatory fines for community members who refuse treatment
options.C: Teaching residents how to identify and clear mosquito breeding sites
options.D: Educating families on safe food storage and personal hygiene habits

explanation: Nurses are educators, caregivers, and advocates. Handing out fines and police enforcement is up to legal authorities, not the nursing team!

question: Why does a lack of health awareness stop patients from insisting on safe injections?

options.A: They have enough money to buy private syringes
options.B: They prefer taking bitter oral medications instead
options.C: They understand hospital sterilization protocols fully
options.D: They do not know what hazards to look out for

explanation: You nailed it. If a patient doesn't know the risks, they won't know what dangerous practices to watch out for or what to demand.

question: What are the three simple action steps in Psychological First Aid (PFA)?

options.A: Assess, Diagnose, and Treat
options.B: Observe, Intervene, and Evaluate
options.C: Search, Rescue, and Stabilize
options.D: Look, Listen, and Link

explanation: Easy to remember: Look for safety, Listen with empathy, and Link people to the help they need. You've got this!

question: Which family caregiver is at the highest risk for caregiver burnout and potentially committing abuse?

options.A: A relative who visits once a week to help with grocery shopping
options.B: A professional nurse who rotates shifts at an assisted living facility
options.C: A spouse who hires a home health aide to assist four hours a day
options.D: An adult child providing 24-hour care alone with no respite support

explanation: Carrying the heavy load 24/7 without a break easily leads to severe burnout. Supporting caregivers is part of holistic nursing!

question: Which patient group requires strict fluid intake and output monitoring?

options.A: Patients taking diuretic medications
options.B: Patients waiting for outpatient eye surgery
options.C: Patients with mild, healing skin scratches
options.D: Patients admitted for routine physical exams

explanation: Diuretics alter fluid excretion, making it necessary to track how much urine the patient passes. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T19#GNS122_U1_T19_h2)

question: Which tiny bone in the middle ear is attached directly to the eardrum?

options.A: Incus
options.B: Cochlea
options.C: Stapes
options.D: Malleus

explanation: The malleus (also known as the hammer) rests right against the eardrum to catch its first vibrations.

question: What role does the involucrum play in chronic bone infection?

options.A: It is the primary channel through which bacteria enter the bloodstream
options.B: It is a soft tissue tumor that mimics bone cancer on an X-ray
options.C: It acts as a sponge that absorbs antibiotics and neutralizes them
options.D: It is new bone formed by the periosteum to wall off the dead bone

explanation: The body creates an outer shell of living new bone called an involucrum around the dead bone segment during the chronic phase. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h3)

question: A patient is prescribed a sustained-release capsule for chronic pain. What must the nurse tell the patient about taking this medication?

options.A: Swallow the capsule whole without chewing or crushing
options.B: Chew the capsule thoroughly before swallowing with water
options.C: Crush the capsule into food if swallowing is difficult
options.D: Open the shell and dissolve the powder in hot water

explanation: Crushing or chewing sustained-release medications destroys their special mechanism and causes a dangerous, immediate release of the entire drug dose. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h2)

question: A nurse is teaching a patient how to collect a sputum sample for testing. Which instruction is best?

options.A: Collect clear saliva immediately after eating a heavy meal
options.B: Rinse the mouth thoroughly with strong antiseptic mouthwash before coughing
options.C: Store the collected container in the domestic refrigerator overnight
options.D: Provide a deep cough sample first thing in the morning

explanation: Brilliant! Early morning deep-cough samples are best because secretions and parasite eggs pool up overnight, making them easier to catch.

question: Why is arthrodesis (joint fusion) rarely performed on major weight-bearing joints like the knee or hip today?

options.A: It requires the client to stay in bed for an entire year.
options.B: It causes severe allergic reactions in most clients.
options.C: It makes the joint grow back larger bone spurs within weeks.
options.D: It permanently eliminates all movement in that joint.

explanation: While fusion successfully stops pain, losing all joint mobility makes walking and normal daily activities extremely difficult. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h7)

question: What is a must-have when introducing a complex new clinical workflow?

options.A: Protected time for staff training during working hours
options.B: Cutting down the number of patient admissions
options.C: Firing senior nurses to save on salaries
options.D: Buying luxury furniture for the breakroom

explanation: Exactly! You can't expect nurses to master new workflows on top of an already crazy shift without giving them dedicated time to learn.

question: Why do many women in Nigeria end up using unsafe abortion methods?

options.A: Strict laws, social stigma, and poor access to safe care
options.B: Surgical facilities are cheap and everywhere
options.C: People just love traditional herbs more than hospitals
options.D: Primary health workers give very clear instructions

explanation: Fear of judgment, legal barriers, and a lack of friendly youth clinics push vulnerable people toward dangerous procedures. Great insight to keep in mind for clinical practice!

question: Which stage of insect development is completely skipped when an insect goes through incomplete metamorphosis?

options.A: The egg stage
options.B: The adult stage
options.C: The pupal stage
options.D: The larval stage

explanation: Incomplete metamorphosis skips the resting pupa stage, moving straight from egg to nymph to adult. Simple and straightforward!

question: How might a partner's attitude cause a client to stop coming for family planning?

options.A: Disapproval or secret opposition can force the client to stop using services quietly
options.B: Supportive partners always pay the clinic staff to cancel appointments
options.C: Involved partners automatically double the efficacy of oral pills
options.D: Partner involvement has no impact on clinic attendance

explanation: Fear of conflict at home can lead clients to quietly drop out. As nurses, creating a safe, confidential space helps us support them through these challenges.

question: Why do prescription medications require a doctor's order?

options.A: They carry higher risks and require medical supervision
options.B: They do not cause any side effects in patients
options.C: They can only be manufactured in hospital pharmacies
options.D: They are always much cheaper than other medications

explanation: Prescription drugs have powerful effects or serious risks that need professional oversight for safe use. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary relationship between a patient's health status and their nutrition?

options.A: Dietary intake only affects surgical patients and nobody else.
options.B: Illness and nutrition have a direct, two-way effect on each other.
options.C: Health status has no real impact on how the body uses food.
options.D: Nutrition only matters after a patient has completely recovered.

explanation: Health status and nutrition influence each other constantly; sickness changes how the body handles nutrients, while poor nutrition worsens illness. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T023#GNS227_U2_T023_h1)

question: Blood type classification represents which type of measurement scale?

options.A: Nominal scale
options.B: Interval scale
options.C: Ordinal scale
options.D: Ratio scale

explanation: Nominal scales deal with named categories that do not have any mathematical order or ranking, such as blood types. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T2#GNS224_U2_T2_h2)

question: A public health nurse wants to measure how many live births occurred per one thousand people in a town over one year. Which rate should be calculated?

options.A: Disease Prevalence Rate
options.B: Crude Birth Rate
options.C: Hospital Admission Ratio
options.D: Maternal Mortality Rate

explanation: The Crude Birth Rate specifically calculates live births per one thousand population in a defined one-year period. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h3)

question: Why is keeping the 'cold chain' so important when handling polio vaccines?

options.A: To activate the chemical preservatives inside the glass vial
options.B: To keep the liquid vaccine from freezing solid in storage
options.C: To prevent the heat-sensitive vaccine from losing its potency
options.D: To ensure the vaccine changes color before administration

explanation: Spot on! Polio vaccines are fragile biological products that break down and become useless if exposed to too much heat.

question: What happens to the white blood cell count during active labour and delivery?

options.A: It surges even higher due to physical stress and tissue trauma
options.B: It drops rapidly to near-zero levels to protect the baby
options.C: It remains completely unchanged throughout the entire process
options.D: It fluctuates wildly based on the mother's blood type

explanation: Labour is hard work! The physical stress causes the white blood cell count to jump up even more right around delivery time.

question: A patient says they feel like a dark curtain or shadow is moving across their vision. What emergency should you suspect?

options.A: Open-angle glaucoma
options.B: Nuclear cataract
options.C: Retinal detachment
options.D: Simple conjunctivitis

explanation: Spot on! That classic 'curtain falling' description is a textbook warning sign that the retina is peeling away from the back of the eye. It's a medical emergency!

question: How do growing follicles signal the brain just before ovulation happens?

options.A: By releasing high levels of estrogen that create a positive feedback loop
options.B: By producing large amounts of progesterone to slow down hormone release
options.C: By stopping all hormonal signals to let the brain rest
options.D: By secreting inhibin to completely block luteinizing hormone production

explanation: As follicles grow, they pump out high levels of estrogen. This switches the body into a positive feedback loop, which sparks the big LH release!

question: Which of the following is NOT a safe condition for a home delivery?

options.A: Singleton pregnancy
options.B: Head-down baby position
options.C: Normal blood pressure
options.D: Placenta previa

explanation: Placenta previa causes severe bleeding and requires immediate hospital management, making home delivery extremely dangerous. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T9#GNS225_U3_T9_h4)

question: What are the specialized sensory receptor cells in the organ of Corti that detect sound called?

options.A: Ossicle cells
options.B: Perilymph cells
options.C: Ganglion cells
options.D: Hair cells

explanation: They are called hair cells because of the tiny hair-like stereocilia on top that bend when fluid moves, turning physical motion into electrical signals.

question: When are outbreaks of water-borne diseases like cholera most common in Nigeria?

options.A: In the middle of the hot dry summer months
options.B: During the rainy season when floods overwhelm sanitation
options.C: Right after major harvesting periods end
options.D: During the dry harmattan season when dust increases

explanation: Heavy rains wash surface waste into shallow wells and boreholes, spreading contamination rapidly during the rainy season. [learn more](GST114_U3_T3#GST114_U3_T3_h7)

question: How is it possible for a patient to be overweight and still suffer from malnutrition?

options.A: Their diet may provide plenty of calories but lack essential micronutrients and protein quality
options.B: Processed foods completely block the stomach from processing any liquids
options.C: Their body refuses to store any energy as fat when they eat processed foods
options.D: Malnutrition only occurs in individuals with extremely low body mass index

explanation: Think of this as 'hidden hunger'—eating plenty of calorie-dense, low-nutrient food means getting heavy calories without the vitamins your body needs.

question: Which nursing action is most important when putting in a urinary catheter?

options.A: Inflating the retention balloon before inserting the tube
options.B: Lubricating only the very tip of the drainage collection bag
options.C: Applying heavy pressure to the lower abdomen while pushing
options.D: Maintaining strict sterile technique throughout the procedure

explanation: Keeping everything super sterile stops nasty germs from hitching a ride up into the bladder and causing a painful infection. Safety first in clinicals!

question: What are the three parts of the epidemiological triangle?

options.A: Infection, immunity, and recovery
options.B: Source, symptom, and treatment
options.C: Vector, parasite, and climate
options.D: Agent, host, and environment

explanation: It's all about the agent causing the trouble, the host carrying it, and the environment bringing them together!

question: Which of these is NOT a correct use of primary clinical space in a healthcare facility?

options.A: Archiving paper medical records that are five years old
options.B: Performing physical examinations and diagnostic assessments
options.C: Providing direct bedside recovery care after surgery
options.D: Administering intravenous medications in a treatment bay

explanation: Clinical space is precious and meant for treating patients! Storing old paper files belongs in a record room, not where active patient care happens.

question: What is the primary goal when treating a patient with anaemia?

options.A: To identify and treat the underlying cause
options.B: To permanently stop all dietary iron intake
options.C: To permanently increase the white blood cell count
options.D: To lower the body temperature to resting levels

explanation: You can't just slap a band-aid on anaemia! Finding out *why* it's happening—whether it's blood loss, heavy periods, or poor nutrition—is key to fixing it.

question: What temperature range is known as the 'danger zone' where food safety is at risk?

options.A: Above 100°C
options.B: Between 0°C and 10°C
options.C: Below freezing point
options.D: Between 5°C and 60°C

explanation: Correct! Bad bacteria multiply super fast when food hangs out in this 5°C to 60°C danger zone.

question: What type of data is mostly used in explanatory research designs?

options.A: Numerical measurements and statistical testing
options.B: Only handwritten personal diaries from patients
options.C: Random historical fiction books
options.D: Unstructured gossip from hospital hallways

explanation: Well done! Explanatory designs use numbers and statistics to clearly show cause-and-effect links.

question: Why is relying on a management theory better than being purely reactive in a hospital ward?

options.A: It guarantees that no nurse will ever feel stressed or overworked
options.B: It prevents doctors from making medication errors during rounds
options.C: It automatically increases the annual hospital financial budget
options.D: It gives leaders a consistent strategy to handle daily challenges

explanation: Structured theories help leaders plan and solve problems proactively instead of just firefighting daily crises. [learn more](GST321_U1_T3#GST321_U1_T3_h1)

question: What does 'informed consent' mean when planning a home delivery?

options.A: The doctor signs a paper without telling the mother anything
options.B: The family understands the risks and benefits and agrees voluntarily
options.C: The government forces every woman to give birth at home
options.D: The traditional birth attendant makes all decisions for the family

explanation: Informed consent requires that patients are fully aware of what they are choosing and agree of their own free will. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h8)

question: What is the primary danger associated with myxedema coma?

options.A: Severe hypoventilation and decreasing mental status
options.B: Unchecked high blood pressure causing cerebral hemorrhage
options.C: Sudden uncontrollable muscle spasms and bone fractures
options.D: Massive fluid overload leading to acute pulmonary edema

explanation: Well done! Myxedema coma slows body systems down so drastically that breathing becomes dangerously shallow or fails altogether.

question: How should removable dentures be kept when the patient is not wearing them?

options.A: Wrapped up tight in dry gauze inside a bedside drawer
options.B: In a labeled container filled with water or soaking solution
options.C: Dropped in boiling water overnight to kill all germs
options.D: Left out in the open air on top of the locker table

explanation: Keeping dentures wet in a safe container stops the plastic material from bending out of shape and keeps them ready for use.

question: An ovarian cancer that is strictly staying inside the ovaries and hasn't spread is at what stage?

options.A: Stage III
options.B: Stage I
options.C: Stage II
options.D: Stage IV

explanation: Correct! Stage I means the cancer is still completely contained within one or both ovaries.

question: Why should a patient avoid putting lotion on their residual limb before wearing a shrinker sock?

options.A: Oily substances make the prosthesis slide off during walking exercises.
options.B: Lotion dissolves the elastic fibers inside the special compression bandage.
options.C: Trapped moisture creates a breeding ground for bacteria and skin breakdown.
options.D: Moisturizers stop the surgical incision from closing completely.

explanation: Lotion plus a tight wrap equals a warm, wet space where bacteria and fungi love to grow. Keeping the skin clean and dry prevents rashes and breakdown!

question: What is a major danger of excessive cohesiveness in a healthcare team?

options.A: Groupthink, where dangerous errors might be ignored to keep peace
options.B: Complete lack of interest in patient outcomes
options.C: Constant fighting and failure to complete basic patient care tasks
options.D: Excessive individual competition among staff nurses

explanation: When teams become too cohesive, members may avoid speaking up against bad ideas to prevent conflict. [learn more](GST321_U7_T1#GST321_U7_T1_h4)

question: A patient has an infected wound on their right hand and notices tender lumps in their right armpit. What does this mean?

options.A: The patient has a primary blood disorder originating in the spleen
options.B: The patient is experiencing normal side effects of red blood cell breakdown
options.C: Bacteria from the hand wound are traveling through lymph vessels to the axillary nodes
options.D: Blockage of the thoracic duct has caused fluid backup in the upper extremity

explanation: Lymph drains from specific regions of the body to nearby nodes. An infection in the hand travels up the arm vessels, causing the armpit (axillary) nodes to trap the germs and swell up.

question: The AED just delivered a shock to your patient. What is the very next thing your team should do?

options.A: Resume high-quality chest compressions immediately
options.B: Remove the AED pads and prepare to transport the patient
options.C: Wait for the device to automatically perform a second analysis
options.D: Check the carotid artery for a strong pulse for one minute

explanation: Don't wait! Right after a shock, jump straight back into chest compressions. Let the AED guide you when it's time for the next rhythm check.

question: What is the main goal of supporting a patient with their medication routine for a chronic illness?

options.A: Reducing the workload of the hospital records department
options.B: Forcing the patient to purchase expensive imported vitamins
options.C: Preventing the patient from asking questions about their care
options.D: Helping the patient take medications correctly and consistently

explanation: Correct! Adherence support is all about encouraging and helping patients stick to their treatment plan so they can get better.

question: How can government tariffs on imported food negatively affect everyday consumers?

options.A: By completely eliminating all local farming jobs in the country
options.B: By lowering the nutritional value of domestically grown crops
options.C: By artificially raising grocery store prices through import taxes
options.D: By forcing farmers to grow fewer nutrient-dense vegetables

explanation: Tariffs add taxes to goods brought in from other countries, driving up final retail prices for shoppers. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h4)

question: What technology does an autoclave use to sterilize medical instruments and waste?

options.A: Pressurized steam
options.B: Dry microwave heat
options.C: Freezing temperatures
options.D: Ultraviolet rays

explanation: Autoclaves use high heat and pressure generated by steam to destroy all microbial life on equipment. [learn more](GST114_U2_T14#GST114_U2_T14_h5)

question: A patient is discouraged because their BMI hasn't budged after starting an exercise routine. What else can you suggest tracking?

options.A: Waist circumference and overall energy levels
options.B: Resting body temperature and pulse rate
options.C: Daily fluid retention and shoe size changes
options.D: Total body height measured twice a week

explanation: Spot on! When starting fitness, patients often swap fat for muscle. Checking waist size and energy levels will often show great progress before the scale moves!

question: What does a general survey primarily evaluate?

options.A: The patient's complete financial and employment history
options.B: The microscopic cellular structure of body tissues
options.C: The patient's overall appearance and obvious behavior
options.D: The exact electrical conduction system of the heart

explanation: The general survey is a quick visual overview of how sick, comfortable, or distressed a patient looks right away. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T3#GNS123_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is the main goal of community mobilisation?

options.A: Empowering people to take action on their own health issues
options.B: Handing down medical instructions from government officials
options.C: Building large hospitals in rural and urban areas
options.D: Providing free prescription drugs to every household

explanation: Community mobilisation focuses on enabling local populations to identify and solve their own health challenges rather than relying entirely on outside help. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h1)

question: Which common blood test checks for both anemia and signs of infection?

options.A: Blood Glucose Test
options.B: Complete Blood Count
options.C: Urinalysis
options.D: Malaria Parasite Test

explanation: A Complete Blood Count (CBC) looks at your red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. It is super helpful for spotting anemia and infections! Keep it up.

question: Why do doctors often give corticosteroids to a mum facing early labor?

options.A: To accelerate fetal lung maturity and reduce breathing difficulties
options.B: To permanently stop all uterine contractions from happening
options.C: To prevent postpartum hemorrhage after delivery
options.D: To lower the mother's blood glucose levels rapidly

explanation: Steroids give a fantastic boost to the baby's developing lungs, helping them avoid serious breathing trouble if they decide to arrive early.

question: What does 'personal liability' mean for you as a registered nurse?

options.A: Obligation to pay taxes on nursing salary directly to the medical board
options.B: Immunity from lawsuits if working inside a government facility
options.C: Accountability for one's own professional actions and nursing care
options.D: Financial responsibility for the entire hospital building and equipment

explanation: Personal liability means you are responsible for your own two hands. If you make a clinical error, you must answer for it individually.

question: A patient develops severe belly pain and a hard, rigid abdomen a few hours after a paracentesis. What could this mean?

options.A: Internal bleeding or bowel perforation
options.B: A mild allergic reaction to the dressing
options.C: Normal healing of the puncture wound
options.D: Successful removal of all ascites fluid

explanation: A hard, painful belly is a red flag! It can point to a serious issue like internal bleeding or an accidental nick in the bowel.

question: How do long-term conditions like diabetes mellitus usually affect our special senses over time?

options.A: They cause sudden and permanent total hearing loss within days.
options.B: They immediately destroy taste buds on the surface of the tongue.
options.C: They prevent the brain from processing any sensory information.
options.D: They slowly damage delicate blood vessels supplying sensory organs.

explanation: Over time, high blood sugar in diabetes slowly damages tiny blood vessels (microvascular damage). This is why chronic conditions often lead to gradual vision changes like retinopathy. You've got this!

question: Why do fungal infections of the toenails (onychomycosis) usually need oral pills instead of just a surface cream?

options.A: Topical creams cannot penetrate deeply enough through the hard nail plate
options.B: Fungi living in toenails are completely immune to all topical antifungal creams
options.C: Topical medications wash away too quickly from the foot due to sweat
options.D: Nail infections are always caused by systemic internal organ failure

explanation: Correct! The nail plate is thick and tough, acting like a shield that surface creams can't pass through. Pills are needed to reach the fungus from within.

question: What does a high dependency ratio mean for a country?

options.A: Every citizen is completely financially independent.
options.B: The government has excess funds for infrastructure projects.
options.C: A small working-age population must support a large number of dependents.
options.D: There are more elderly people than working adults.

explanation: A high dependency ratio means fewer working adults are carrying the financial weight of supporting a large group of children and elderly dependents.

question: Which factor is part of evaluating the home environment for childbirth?

options.A: Size of the family garden
options.B: Presence of a television set
options.C: Reliable source of clean water
options.D: Proximity to a shopping mall

explanation: Clean water is essential for maintaining hygiene, washing hands, and preventing postpartum infections during and after delivery. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T9#GNS225_U3_T9_h6)

question: Why is educating the girl child considered so important for Primary Health Care?

options.A: It equips girls with health literacy and disease prevention knowledge
options.B: It directly increases the annual government health budget
options.C: It eliminates the need for rural health clinics and dispensaries
options.D: It guarantees that every girl will eventually become a certified nurse

explanation: Spot on! When girls go to school, they pick up practical health and hygiene knowledge that helps keep their entire community healthy and safe.

question: A CT scan image shows a cross-section of the abdomen dividing it into top and bottom halves. Which plane was used?

options.A: Transverse
options.B: Sagittal
options.C: Midsagittal
options.D: Coronal

explanation: Think of slicing a loaf of bread! Cross-sections that view the body from top to bottom are produced by cutting along the transverse plane.

question: Why must the delivery room be kept warm and free from cold drafts?

options.A: Cold drafts increase the risk of maternal postpartum bleeding
options.B: Newborn babies quickly lose body heat and cannot shiver
options.C: Cold air causes the mother's uterine contractions to stop
options.D: Warm temperatures help keep delivery instruments sterile longer

explanation: Newborns can't shiver to warm up yet! Keeping the room cozy protects them from rapid heat loss and cold stress right after birth.

question: As a nurse entering a brand new community, what should always be your very first step?

options.A: Listening to the community before telling them what to do
options.B: Demanding that the village head build a new health post
options.C: Distributing medications without proper medical evaluations
options.D: Issuing strict rules on sanitation and personal hygiene

explanation: Brilliant! Listening first shows respect. It helps you understand their everyday realities and priorities before you try to introduce any changes.

question: Why is carbidopa always given alongside levodopa when treating Parkinson's?

options.A: To act as a direct replacement for lost acetylcholine
options.B: To sedate the patient and prevent involuntary tremors
options.C: To prevent the breakdown of levodopa before it reaches the brain
options.D: To completely cure the underlying neuronal degeneration

explanation: Think of carbidopa as the bodyguard for levodopa. It stops levodopa from breaking down too early in the body so that enough of it actually reaches the brain to do its job!

question: During a follow-up visit, you notice a patient missed their nutrition goals. What should you do next?

options.A: Discharge the patient from nutrition education
options.B: Reassess barriers and adjust the plan together
options.C: Double the dietary restrictions immediately
options.D: Scold the patient for lack of self-discipline

explanation: You're developing a wonderful bedside manner! Never blame or scold. Team up with the patient to figure out what went wrong and tweak the plan together. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h7)

question: What is the primary output of the action planning phase?

options.A: A lengthy academic textbook published for university students
options.B: An application for international political asylum
options.C: A detailed schedule of activities, responsibilities, and resources
options.D: A list of punishments for families who violate hygiene laws

explanation: An action plan clearly outlines what tasks need to be done, who is responsible, when it will occur, and what materials are needed. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h6)

question: Besides antibodies, what specific viral marker do fourth-generation HIV tests look for?

options.A: p24 antigen
options.B: Integrase enzyme
options.C: Reverse transcriptase
options.D: gp120 protein

explanation: Awesome work! Fourth-gen tests search for the p24 antigen alongside antibodies, helping us catch recent infections much earlier.

question: Why is a low-residue (low-fiber, easy-to-digest) diet often given during a flare-up of inflammatory bowel disease?

options.A: To prevent the development of high blood pressure and fluid retention
options.B: To provide extra protein necessary for healing surgical incisions
options.C: To minimize mechanical irritation and reduce the workload on the inflamed bowel
options.D: To stimulate rapid weight loss and reduce overall body fat percentage

explanation: Think of it as giving the gut a gentle break. Low-residue foods leave very little waste behind, letting the sore, inflamed intestines rest and recover.

question: If a partner stops you from working and controls all the money in the house, what kind of abuse is that?

options.A: Emotional abuse
options.B: Economic abuse
options.C: Sexual abuse
options.D: Physical abuse

explanation: Correct! Economic abuse happens when someone cuts off another person's access to money or financial independence to trap them.

question: How does assertive behavior differ from aggressive behavior?

options.A: Assertiveness requires shouting to be heard clearly
options.B: Aggression is used exclusively by senior nursing staff
options.C: Assertiveness attacks the issue rather than the person
options.D: Aggression always leads to better patient outcomes

explanation: While aggression targets and belittles individuals, assertiveness keeps the focus firmly on solving the professional problem. [learn more](GST321_U7_T5#GST321_U7_T5_h1)

question: What is the main goal of health advocacy in community nursing?

options.A: To raise private funds for hospital equipment purchases
options.B: To replace individual clinical treatments with community meetings
options.C: To increase the daily working hours of primary health nurses
options.D: To shift community attitudes and change policies for better health

explanation: You've got this! Advocacy is all about looking at the big picture—changing policies and mindsets to fix health problems at their root, rather than just treating patients one by one.

question: What sign makes a Type 2 leprosy reaction (ENL) different from a Type 1 reaction?

options.A: Crops of painful, tender subcutaneous red nodules across the body
options.B: Slow fading of existing hypopigmented patches over several months
options.C: Complete absence of systemic symptoms like fever and joint aches
options.D: Sudden loss of motor function without any associated skin changes

explanation: Spot on! Type 2 reactions bring along painful red bumps under the skin (ENL) plus fever and body aches.

question: What is the main goal of purposive sampling in qualitative studies?

options.A: Choosing people randomly from a large national census list
options.B: Ensuring every person in the hospital has an equal chance to join
options.C: Selecting participants who have direct experience with the topic
options.D: Finding participants who disagree with the researcher's hypothesis

explanation: Exactly! 'Purposive' means on purpose—you pick people who actually lived the experience so they can give you the best information.

question: A patient recovering from a thyroid surgery reports numbness and tingling around their lips and fingers. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Encourage the patient to drink a large glass of calcium-fortified milk
options.B: Assess for signs of neuromuscular irritability like Trousseau's sign
options.C: Reassure the patient that postoperative anxiety is completely normal
options.D: Administer a stat dose of oral potassium chloride syrup

explanation: Numbness and tingling around the mouth are classic early red flags for low calcium (hypocalcemia) after neck surgery. Always assess further right away!

question: Which of these is NOT a good self-care practice for managing long-term leg swelling?

options.A: Wearing tight, restrictive garters to keep the swelling squeezed down
options.B: Elevating the legs periodically throughout the day
options.C: Following a reduced-sodium diet as prescribed by the doctor
options.D: Inspecting the lower legs daily for any skin breaks or redness

explanation: Spot on! Avoid tight bands or restrictive garters because they actually choke off circulation and make fluid pooling worse. Proper medical compression stockings should be used instead!

question: Your hospital ward gets flooded with sudden admissions, leaving you short-staffed. What is the best way to handle patient safety?

options.A: Cancel all routine documentation and vitals checks for the entire day
options.B: Refuse admission to all incoming patients until the next shift arrives
options.C: Increase out-of-pocket treatment prices to immediately lower patient demand
options.D: Adjust staff assignments and prioritize urgent clinical care needs

explanation: Brilliant clinical thinking! When hands are few, a good nurse reorganizes tasks, focusing heavily on those whose lives are most at risk.

question: What is the main goal of evaluating population health programs?

options.A: To write promotional brochures for the local government ministry
options.B: To find staff members to blame when a project runs out of money
options.C: To increase the cost of medical services for community residents
options.D: To determine whether the health interventions actually achieved their intended goals

explanation: Evaluation measures the real-world impact of health programs so nurses know what is working and what needs improvement. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h7)

question: What does 'myelosuppression' mean?

options.A: A sudden swelling of the lymph nodes in the neck
options.B: An infection located directly on the outer layer of the skin
options.C: The suppression of blood cell production in the bone marrow
options.D: The overproduction of red blood cells in the bone marrow

explanation: Big medical word, simple meaning! It just means cancer treatments slow down bone marrow activity, leading to low blood counts. You're learning fast!

question: Which of the following must always be included when documenting a critical finding in a patient chart?

options.A: The personal opinion of the nurse about the patient's family
options.B: The name of every nurse working in the hospital
options.C: The exact cost of the diagnostic tests ordered
options.D: The exact time the finding was reported to the doctor

explanation: Recording the time of notification is legally crucial to prove timely communication and action during a medical emergency. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T2#GNS213_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why does handing out certificates fail if a manager ignores broken equipment and chronic understaffing?

options.A: Because hygiene factors like basic working conditions must be addressed first
options.B: Because nurses only care about financial bonuses and nothing else
options.C: Because certificates decrease the intrinsic drive of veteran nurses
options.D: Because recognition programs are illegal in most healthcare settings

explanation: Paper awards can't fix a stressful environment with broken gear and too few hands. Basic working conditions must be sorted out first!

question: What is the first thing a nurse should check before starting a teaching session?

options.A: The cost of printing handouts
options.B: The personal hobbies of the patient
options.C: The patient's readiness to learn
options.D: The availability of colorful posters

explanation: Spot on! If a patient is in severe pain or exhausted, teaching won't stick. Always check if they are ready first.

question: What does a negative correlation look like on a scatter diagram?

options.A: Dots trend downward from left to right
options.B: Dots form a flat horizontal straight line
options.C: Dots trend upward from left to right
options.D: Dots are scattered randomly everywhere

explanation: Think of it like going downhill: as one variable goes up, the other goes down, creating a downward slope from left to right.

question: Why must nurses look beyond just treating symptoms when managing a patient with a waterborne illness?

options.A: To test the structural strength of local concrete septic tanks
options.B: To identify and correct the underlying environmental exposure source
options.C: To calculate the financial cost of repairing city water pumps
options.D: To obtain government permits for building new treatment plants

explanation: Treating the illness is only half the battle. If the patient goes back to drinking contaminated water, they will just get sick again. Nurses look at the big picture to fix the root cause!

question: A client on a weight-loss diet says they are always hungry and haven't lost any weight after four weeks. What should you do?

options.A: Tell the client to stop eating all solid food until the next appointment
options.B: Discharge the client from care for failing to lose weight
options.C: Review the current food intake and adjust the plan collaboratively with the client
options.D: Ignore the feedback because four weeks is not enough time to evaluate

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! Sit down with the patient, figure out what's blocking progress together, and tweak the plan so it actually works for them.

question: Why might wild, erratic vital sign readings with high variability point to a clinical emergency?

options.A: High variability always proves that the sensor equipment is broken
options.B: A steady high reading is always more dangerous than fluctuating numbers
options.C: Unstable fluctuations often signal that homeostatic mechanisms are failing
options.D: Monitors are programmed to sound alarms whenever data is perfectly stable

explanation: When the body's natural balance (homeostasis) starts failing, vital signs bounce all over the place. High variability is often a red flag for a crashing patient!

question: What is the difference between a normal drug side effect and an adverse drug reaction (ADR)?

options.A: It is completely harmless and requires no intervention
options.B: It is a harmful and unintended response at normal doses
options.C: It is always an expected pharmacological outcome
options.D: It only happens when a patient takes an overdose

explanation: Think of an ADR as an unwanted, harmful surprise that happens even when you give the exact right dose. You've got this!

question: A mother says she mixed her child's ORS packet into half a liter of water instead of a full liter. What should you do?

options.A: Advise her to add extra sugar to balance out the high salt content
options.B: Instruct her to add another half-liter of water to the existing mixture and stir well
options.C: Allow her to feed the concentrated solution since it will work faster anyway
options.D: Discard the solution and help her mix a fresh batch correctly with one full liter of water

explanation: Guessing water amounts can throw off body chemistry. It is always safest to throw out the wrong mix and prepare a fresh, accurately measured batch.

question: How does breaking big, complicated tasks into tiny steps help a patient with a degenerative condition?

options.A: It speeds up the rate of cognitive processing in the brain
options.B: It ensures the patient never needs assistance from family members
options.C: It prevents feelings of overwhelming helplessness and promotes a sense of control
options.D: It cures the underlying muscle weakness completely

explanation: Mini-steps make daily activities feel doable rather than scary, helping patients hold onto their independence and confidence.

question: Why do the remaining healthy nephrons get larger (hypertrophy) during the early stages of chronic kidney disease?

options.A: To produce extra urine that completely flushes out all uremic toxins from the body
options.B: To increase blood pressure so that the heart pumps faster to the extremities
options.C: To compensate for the workload of the nephrons that have already been destroyed
options.D: To store extra electrolytes and vitamins for future metabolic needs

explanation: Think of it like a team picking up extra shifts when coworkers drop out. Healthy nephrons try to take over the filtering work, but this extra strain eventually causes them to burn out too.

question: A nurse is caring for a patient with end-stage kidney disease. Which sign is most directly linked to the kidneys losing their hormone-making job?

options.A: Rapid digestion of proteins in the stomach
options.B: High levels of vitamin B12 in the blood
options.C: Severe fatigue and low hemoglobin
options.D: Excessive production of digestive bile

explanation: You nailed it! Low hemoglobin and constant tiredness are classic signs of anemia because the kidneys aren't making enough EPO anymore.

question: What is the main difference between the scope of practice of an LPN and a home health aide?

options.A: LPNs only handle housekeeping duties while aides manage complex wounds
options.B: Aides are licensed to supervise registered nurses in the home setting
options.C: LPNs can perform routine clinical tasks like giving medications, while aides focus on personal care
options.D: There is no difference in training or clinical responsibilities

explanation: LPNs have nursing training that allows them to handle basic clinical interventions, whereas home health aides are restricted to personal support tasks. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h3)

question: What does population health nursing primarily focus on?

options.A: The financial balance sheet of a health clinic
options.B: The health outcomes of an entire group of people
options.C: The surgical procedures performed in a single hospital ward
options.D: The genetic profile of an individual patient

explanation: Population health looks beyond the individual patient to protect and promote the well-being of whole communities. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h1)

question: A study tests if a new low-salt diet lowers blood pressure in hypertensive patients. What is the independent variable?

options.A: The patient's blood pressure
options.B: The hospital reading room
options.C: The patient's age and weight
options.D: The low-salt diet

explanation: The independent variable is the intervention or action introduced by the researcher—in this case, the special diet.

question: Which of these is a mistake to avoid when translating IEC materials for a local community?

options.A: Translating the message into the primary local language of the community
options.B: Using clear local symbols and pictorial representations
options.C: Using literal word-for-word translation without checking local meaning
options.D: Involving local community leaders to explain key terms

explanation: Word-for-word translations can completely twist the meaning of health instructions. Always check how locals actually say it!

question: Why is it often hard to convince patients to take their blood pressure pills every single day?

options.A: Antihypertensive drugs taste extremely sweet.
options.B: Blood pressure medications only work during the rainy season.
options.C: Pills are too large to swallow comfortably.
options.D: Patients often feel fine and may not see the need to take drugs daily.

explanation: Spot on! Because high blood pressure usually doesn't make people feel sick day-to-day, they might mistakenly think they don't need their meds.

question: Why must you confirm a bed is ready at the receiving hospital before you even launch the evacuation?

options.A: To ensure the transport vehicle has enough fuel for the trip
options.B: To let the pilot know which runway is clear for landing
options.C: To calculate the exact financial cost of the hospital stay
options.D: To prevent dangerous delays upon arrival at the destination

explanation: Arriving at a busy hospital with no bed ready wastes precious time and leaves your vulnerable patient stuck waiting inside the transport vehicle.

question: Which part of the nephron reabsorbs the biggest share of filtered bicarbonate?

options.A: Loop of Henle
options.B: Distal convoluted tubule
options.C: Collecting duct
options.D: Proximal convoluted tubule

explanation: You've got this! The proximal convoluted tubule is the hardworking champion that reclaims the vast majority of filtered bicarbonate right back into the bloodstream.

question: Why don't petechiae and purpura turn white when you press your finger on them?

options.A: Blood has leaked entirely outside the blood vessels into the tissue
options.B: The underlying capillaries are permanently dilated from heat
options.C: The skin has become too thick from chronic scratching
options.D: There is an overproduction of clear serum inside the blister

explanation: Since the red blood cells have escaped right out into the skin tissue, pressing on top won't make the color go away.

question: Which of these is NOT something a modern family planning nurse should do?

options.A: Reaching out to adolescents with friendly reproductive education
options.B: Promoting personalized contraceptive choices for patients
options.C: Forcing universal sterilization on rural communities
options.D: Expanding access to long-acting reversible contraceptives

explanation: Forced procedures go totally against human rights and good nursing. Care should always be voluntary and centered on what the patient wants!

question: What do we mean when we talk about a drug's 'affinity'?

options.A: The time it takes for a drug to dissolve
options.B: The attraction between a drug and its receptor
options.C: The total amount of drug excreted in urine
options.D: The speed at which the liver metabolizes a drug

explanation: Affinity is basically how strongly a drug 'likes' and sticks to its specific receptor. High affinity means a tight, cozy fit!

question: What is the main job of Montgomery's tubercles on the areola during pregnancy and breastfeeding?

options.A: To regulate the release of prolactin from the pituitary gland
options.B: To contract and push milk forward into the lactiferous ducts
options.C: To produce the first wave of thick yellow colostrum
options.D: To secrete an oily substance that protects and lubricates the nipple

explanation: Those little bumps on the areola (Montgomery's glands) act like a natural moisturizer, keeping the skin healthy and ready for feeding. Great job learning the anatomy!

question: Which syringe and needle setup is best for giving a Mantoux skin test?

options.A: A 1-mL tuberculin syringe with a short 27-gauge fine needle
options.B: A 5-mL syringe with a blunt-tip drawing needle
options.C: An insulin syringe marked in units with a permanent attached needle
options.D: A 3-mL syringe with a large 21-gauge intramuscular needle

explanation: You need a tiny syringe to measure tiny drops accurately, and a short, fine needle helps you slide the fluid right into the top layers of the skin! [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h3)

question: What does the term 'medicalization' mean when talking about female genital mutilation?

options.A: Treating FGM infections in a hospital setting
options.B: Having a trained healthcare worker perform the cutting procedure
options.C: Doing scientific research on how common the practice is
options.D: Using modern pain relief during traditional cutting

explanation: You're on point! Medicalization refers to the harmful practice of health workers performing FGM under the false belief that clinical tools make it safe.

question: What is the primary purpose of using supportive devices like pillows and trochanter rolls?

options.A: To prevent the patient from speaking
options.B: To increase patient body temperature
options.C: To maintain correct body alignment
options.D: To speed up intravenous infusion rates

explanation: Supportive devices keep joints in a natural, neutral position to prevent deformities like footdrop and muscle strain. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h1)

question: Why do medications absorb very slowly from the dermal layer of the skin?

options.A: The epidermis blocks most medications from entering.
options.B: Sweat glands actively wash the medication away.
options.C: Skin cells in the dermis are tightly packed together.
options.D: The dermis has a very limited blood supply.

explanation: Limited blood vessels in the dermis mean the drug stays localized and is picked up very gradually by the body. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why should nurses always focus on 'felt needs' (real problems the community faces daily) when planning education?

options.A: It guarantees immediate financial funding from donors
options.B: It prevents nurses from having to prepare visual aids
options.C: Learners pay closer attention to problems they actually experience
options.D: Government policy requires ignoring community complaints

explanation: People naturally care more about health issues affecting their everyday lives than abstract or distant theories.

question: What is the main danger when food or liquid silently slips into a patient's lungs without them even coughing?

options.A: Development of aspiration pneumonia
options.B: Immediate complete upper airway blockage
options.C: Rapid electrolyte imbalance and dehydration
options.D: Sudden severe allergic skin rashes

explanation: When foreign material and mouth bacteria sneak down into the lungs, they set up camp and cause a nasty infection known as aspiration pneumonia. Always stay alert!

question: What is the main difference between nutritional screening and a full nutritional assessment?

options.A: Screening is done by doctors, while assessment is done by cooks
options.B: Screening is only used for children, while assessment is for adults
options.C: Screening is a quick check to find risk, while assessment is a deep dive
options.D: Screening only looks at lab work, while assessment only looks at weight

explanation: Screening quickly identifies who is at risk, prompting a thorough assessment to diagnose specific nutritional problems. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T001#GNS227_U5_T001_h4)

question: How were early population control programs different from modern reproductive rights?

options.A: Early programs focused exclusively on treating infertility rather than contraception
options.B: Modern frameworks rely on government-mandated family sizes to reduce poverty
options.C: Modern frameworks ignore maternal health in favor of economic development
options.D: Early programs prioritized national demographic targets over individual bodily autonomy

explanation: In the past, programs often focused on hitting government population numbers. Today, we focus on respecting each person's individual rights and personal choices.

question: What key lesson did the world learn from successful global vaccination campaigns against smallpox?

options.A: Coordinated international public health strategies can eradicate major diseases
options.B: Vaccines are only effective inside sterile hospital operating rooms
options.C: Local communities cannot participate in disease prevention
options.D: Infectious diseases disappear naturally without human intervention

explanation: Teamwork works! Smallpox proved that when the whole world joins forces on immunization, we can wipe out deadly diseases.

question: What can happen if a nursing research study uses a sample size that is far too small?

options.A: The statistical software will refuse to run any calculations
options.B: Every patient in the hospital will be forced to participate
options.C: The researcher might miss a real and important clinical effect
options.D: The study will automatically cost too much money to complete

explanation: Spot on! If your group of patients is too tiny, your study won't have enough power to spot a real pattern or treatment benefit.

question: What is the primary purpose of a downward referral in mental health?

options.A: To clear hospital beds by discharging clients without any follow-up plan
options.B: To transfer chronic cases to out-of-state traditional healing homes
options.C: To return stabilized clients to community clinics for ongoing maintenance care
options.D: To punish clients who refuse to take part in group therapy sessions

explanation: Downward referral steps patients down to community care once they are stable, freeing up specialist beds while keeping them supported close to home.

question: Where does a water-soluble peptide hormone need to bind to send its message to a target cell?

options.A: Directly to DNA inside the cell nucleus
options.B: To a receptor on the outer cell membrane
options.C: To free-floating ribosomes in the cytoplasm
options.D: To transport proteins inside the blood vessel

explanation: Since water-soluble hormones can't cross the oily cell membrane, they have to knock on the outside door by binding to surface receptors to pass along their message.

question: What is the main job of the effector in a homeostatic loop?

options.A: To carry out the final response that alters the internal environment
options.B: To constantly measure the exact temperature of the skin
options.C: To process signals and decide if a change is dangerous
options.D: To store excess glucose until the body needs extra fuel

explanation: Great job! Effectors are the doers—like muscles or sweat glands—that take the instructions and actually fix the imbalance in the body.

question: What is the primary overarching goal of Nigeria's National Population Policy?

options.A: Halting all immigration into the country immediately
options.B: Reducing the national literacy rate to save government funds
options.C: Eliminating the entire rural population through urbanization
options.D: Improving the standard of living and quality of life for citizens

explanation: At its heart, every goal in the population policy is about making sure citizens live healthier, better-quality lives by balancing population growth with available resources.

question: Why is community ownership critical for the success of a health project?

options.A: It ensures the community will sustain the project after external aid ends
options.B: It removes the need for any financial planning or budgeting
options.C: It guarantees that no one in the village will ever fall sick again
options.D: It allows nurses to stop visiting the community entirely

explanation: When people own a project, they care for it and keep it running long after outside organisations leave. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h1)

question: What body tissue is the primary driver of a person's metabolic rate?

options.A: Bone mineral matrix
options.B: Subcutaneous water
options.C: Adipose fat tissue
options.D: Lean muscle mass

explanation: Muscle tissue burns significantly more calories at rest than fat tissue, making muscle mass the main driver of metabolism. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h4)

question: Which quick test is most commonly used at the bedside to check for a collapsed lung?

options.A: Chest X-ray
options.B: Magnetic resonance imaging
options.C: Pulmonary function testing
options.D: Bronchoscopy

explanation: A quick chest X-ray gives us an immediate picture of what's going on inside the chest cavity. Keep up the great diagnostic thinking!

question: What is the name for the separate little lobes found on the maternal side of the placenta?

options.A: Cotyledons
options.B: Villi
options.C: Decidua
options.D: Chorions

explanation: You'll look for these 15 to 20 sections, called cotyledons, during your midwifery clinicals to make sure the placenta came out completely! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T6#GNS121_U6_T6_h1)

question: Why is clear paperwork and documentation so important when transferring a patient to a teaching hospital?

options.A: To prove to the hospital management that nurses are working hard
options.B: To increase the hospital billing charges for the patient
options.C: To ensure continuity of care and prevent treatment delays
options.D: To make the patient's folder look bulky and professional

explanation: Good transfer notes give the new team a clear history of what has been done, making sure the patient keeps getting safe, uninterrupted care without repeating tests.

question: For which age group of pregnancy are steroids routinely recommended if early birth threatens?

options.A: Post-term only
options.B: 38 to 42 weeks
options.C: 24 to 34 weeks
options.D: 16 to 20 weeks

explanation: Babies born between 24 and 34 weeks benefit the absolute most from these lung-maturing steroids. You're storing up great clinical facts for your exams and wards!

question: What do we call a neuron that has one main axon and many dendrites branching out?

options.A: Unipolar neuron
options.B: Anaxonic neuron
options.C: Multipolar neuron
options.D: Bipolar neuron

explanation: Since it has multiple extensions (one axon plus many dendrites), it's called a multipolar neuron. These are the most common type in our nervous system!

question: During which stage of an infection do mild, general symptoms like tiredness first show up before full sickness hits?

options.A: Incubation period
options.B: Prodromal stage
options.C: Convalescent stage
options.D: Illness stage

explanation: Well done! The prodromal stage is that early phase where a patient just feels 'off' or unusually tired before specific symptoms appear.

question: Which of these is an example of a direct medical cost?

options.A: Lodging for family members
options.B: Hospital parking fees
options.C: Prescription medications
options.D: Bus fare to clinic visits

explanation: Prescription drugs are directly tied to treating the patient's illness, making them a direct medical cost.

question: Why must nurses change bed linens with extra care during Gallows traction?

options.A: To stop the baby from rolling onto their stomach
options.B: To keep the fracture and traction setup perfectly aligned
options.C: To keep the weights from breaking
options.D: To save money on hospital laundry

explanation: Any sudden shake can disturb the healing bone and cause great pain. Smooth, careful movements are key!

question: What happens if a patient uses over-the-counter medicated nasal sprays for too many days in a row?

options.A: Rebound nasal congestion
options.B: Severe fungal ear infections
options.C: Systemic high blood pressure
options.D: Permanent loss of the sense of smell

explanation: Exactly! Overusing these sprays causes the blood vessels in the nose to swell right back up even worse once the drug wears off.

question: Which health history complaint needs an urgent neurological check right away?

options.A: Occasional muscle cramps after heavy exercise
options.B: Sudden changes in speech and vision
options.C: Temporary skin dryness in cold weather
options.D: Mild fatigue after a full night of sleep

explanation: Sudden trouble talking or seeing are major warning signs for a stroke or another urgent brain emergency. Always stay alert for these!

question: Taking a patient's height, weight, and body mass index (BMI) falls under which type of assessment?

options.A: Environmental data review
options.B: Clinical physical inspection
options.C: Anthropometric measurement
options.D: Biochemical laboratory test

explanation: Spot on! "Anthropometric" is just the clinical term for measuring the size, weight, and proportions of the human body.

question: When should the nurse verify the placement of a nasogastric tube?

options.A: Whenever the patient complains of a headache
options.B: Once a week on the morning shift
options.C: Before every fluid instillation or medication dose
options.D: Only once immediately after initial insertion

explanation: Tubes can shift out of place easily, so checking placement before putting anything down the tube protects the airway. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T3#GNS213_U3_T3_h7)

question: Why do nursing students need to learn about different sources of knowledge?

options.A: To eliminate the need for clinical experience entirely
options.B: To memorize every historical medical text ever written
options.C: To understand why clinical guidelines change and why evidence matters
options.D: To learn how to diagnose patients without a doctor

explanation: Knowing where knowledge comes from helps you see why nursing care changes for the better as new evidence comes to light. You've got this!

question: What is the main reason regulatory bodies like the NMCN oversee nursing practice?

options.A: To protect the public from substandard practice and ensure legal compliance
options.B: To fund the construction of private residential houses
options.C: To supply free medications directly to nursing homes
options.D: To handle international travel arrangements for nurses

explanation: Regulatory bodies exist to set clear professional boundaries, ensuring every nurse maintains safe standards to protect the public. Great job!

question: Why do many young females struggle to insist on barrier protection like condoms during sex?

options.A: A lack of physical strength to hold the protective devices
options.B: Medical regulations prohibiting females from purchasing supplies
options.C: Power imbalances and fear of financial or physical retribution
options.D: Biological immunity that makes protection completely unnecessary

explanation: Exactly. When a partner holds all the power—or threatens violence—safe sex negotiation becomes terrifyingly difficult.

question: What piece of info is automatically attached to every single entry you make in an EMR?

options.A: The brand name of the computer monitor used
options.B: The patient's bank account and credit score
options.C: The user login ID, date, and exact timestamp
options.D: The GPS coordinates of the hospital building

explanation: Digital charts automatically stamp your notes with metadata, proving precisely who entered the information and when.

question: When giving a bed bath, which direction should you always wash the patient's body?

options.A: From the legs up straight to the face
options.B: From the sides toward the back spine
options.C: From the most sensitive parts to the least sensitive
options.D: From the cleanest areas to the dirtiest areas

explanation: Brilliant! Always start with the cleanest parts (like the face) and move down so you don't drag dirt and germs onto clean skin.

question: How is a research report different from a regular story essay?

options.A: It avoids using references or formal citations
options.B: It relies heavily on empirical data and structured formatting
options.C: It is always written in the first person narrative style
options.D: It focuses primarily on fictional clinical scenarios

explanation: Think of a research report as a neat, structured map of proven facts rather than a casual diary entry. You're doing great!

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to mental health referrals in Nigeria?

options.A: High cost of transportation and out-of-pocket treatment expenses
options.B: Poor communication and missing feedback letters between facilities
options.C: Stigma and initial reliance on traditional or spiritual healers
options.D: Immediate availability of fully equipped psychiatric units in every rural village

explanation: Spot the trick! Fully equipped psychiatric units in every rural village definitely do not exist, making this option the false statement—and thus the correct answer.

question: Which embryonic germ layer develops into the nervous system and the outer skin?

options.A: Trophoblast
options.B: Endoderm
options.C: Ectoderm
options.D: Mesoderm

explanation: You nailed it! The ectoderm is the outer layer, making things that help us sense and interact with the outside world, like skin and nerves.

question: What does self-medication mean in everyday healthcare?

options.A: Receiving free drug samples directly from a licensed hospital pharmacist
options.B: Sharing prescribed drugs strictly among family members living in the same house
options.C: Taking medications without a prescription from a qualified practitioner
options.D: Buying herbal teas from registered supermarkets for general wellness

explanation: Spot on! Self-medication simply means taking drugs without getting professional guidance or a valid prescription first.

question: Which of these is NOT a main job of the cardiovascular system?

options.A: Moving nutrients throughout the body
options.B: Transporting oxygen to tissues
options.C: Producing digestive enzymes
options.D: Carrying carbon dioxide away from cells

explanation: Digestive enzymes are made by organs in your digestive system, like the pancreas and stomach, not your heart and blood vessels!

question: What is the everyday clinical nickname for a bag-valve-mask device?

options.A: Suction catheter
options.B: Venturi mask
options.C: Ambu bag
options.D: Nebulizer

explanation: You will hear nurses and doctors call this the 'Ambu bag' all the time on the ward. It's your best friend in an emergency!

question: Why is the intravenous route preferred over oral medications during a severe medical emergency?

options.A: It is completely painless for the patient
options.B: It prevents the kidneys from filtering drugs
options.C: It provides immediate bioavailability
options.D: It completely avoids the need for a nurse

explanation: Injecting medication directly into the vein skips absorption time, making it act instantly when seconds matter. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T5#GNS125_U3_T5_h1)

question: If a patient just had surgery, which food category is most important to help close up that incision?

options.A: Energy-giving foods
options.B: Protective foods
options.C: Body-building foods
options.D: Perishable foods

explanation: You nailed it! Body-building foods are rich in proteins, which act like bricks and mortar to fix cut tissues and heal wounds.

question: Which of the following is an environmental hazard commonly checked during a home visit?

options.A: The type of flooring material in the kitchen
options.B: The color of paint used on the bedroom walls
options.C: Cluttered walkways and poor lighting
options.D: The brand of television in the living room

explanation: Physical hazards like clutter and poor lighting increase the risk of falls and injuries, especially for vulnerable clients. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T6#GNS314_U4_T6_h4)

question: Why is community engagement critical for the success of quarantine protocols?

options.A: It replaces the need for any medical supplies in the treatment centers.
options.B: It builds trust and reduces resistance or hiding of symptoms.
options.C: It guarantees that no one will ever catch the disease again.
options.D: It allows health workers to skip daily temperature monitoring.

explanation: Engaging the community fosters cooperation and prevents people from evading public health restrictions due to fear or misunderstanding. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h8)

question: Why are certain populations classified as high-risk groups for unsafe injections?

options.A: They metabolize injectable drugs much slower than other people
options.B: They always refuse standard vaccination programs in rural clinics
options.C: They have higher exposure to contaminated needles or biological fluids
options.D: They lack basic knowledge about oral medication administration

explanation: High-risk groups face a greater chance of harm because their daily routines or health conditions put them near contaminated equipment. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T5#GNS122_U3_T5_h1)

question: Why must calcium bind to troponin before a muscle can contract?

options.A: It directly provides the energy needed for the power stroke
options.B: It moves tropomyosin away from actin binding sites
options.C: It holds the Z-lines firmly in place during movement
options.D: It destroys excess acetylcholine in the synapse

explanation: At rest, tropomyosin blocks the binding sites like a locked door. Calcium acts as the key that shifts it out of the way so the muscle can get to work! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T12#GNS121_U3_T12_h5)

question: Why do people trying to quit smoking often get sudden cravings when doing routine things, like drinking morning tea?

options.A: Their physical lungs are suddenly damaged by the beverage steam
options.B: The brain has formed strong behavioral links between those routines and smoking
options.C: Their immune system is reacting to dietary changes
options.D: The tea contains hidden traces of chemical nicotine

explanation: Daily habits act as triggers because the brain links those routines directly to smoking. Recognizing this helps us support patients better!

question: A patient says they drink strong cough syrup containing codeine every day just to chill and relax. What is happening here?

options.A: Proper management of a chronic upper respiratory infection
options.B: Substance misuse and potential psychological dependence
options.C: An effective strategy to build natural immunity against colds
options.D: A harmless alternative to sleeping pills

explanation: Well done! Using codeine-lacking syrups just for a high or relaxation leads straight down the road to substance abuse and addiction.

question: Why is your Eustachian tube so important?

options.A: Translating vibrations into nerve signals
options.B: Secreting protective earwax
options.C: Equalizing air pressure in the middle ear
options.D: Amplifying high-pitched sounds

explanation: Ever felt your ears 'pop' when swallowing or yawning? That is your Eustachian tube balancing out air pressure so your eardrum stays comfortable.

question: What is the main difference between a medical emergency and a surgical emergency?

options.A: Surgical emergencies never require any medication, whereas medical emergencies always require an immediate operation
options.B: Medical emergencies usually involve internal system failure treated with drugs, while surgical emergencies involve physical damage requiring an operation
options.C: Medical emergencies only happen to children, while surgical emergencies only happen to elderly patients
options.D: There is no difference in how nurses manage medical and surgical emergency cases

explanation: Think of it this way: medical crises focus on internal illness managed with medicine, while surgical emergencies need an operation in the theatre to fix physical damage. Great job working through this!

question: What does the tech phrase 'garbage in, garbage out' mean for nursing documentation?

options.A: All hospital trash must be sorted before entering the electronic system
options.B: Inaccurate data entry leads to unreliable clinical reports and decisions
options.C: Patient records must be printed and thrown away every evening
options.D: Computers automatically delete any notes typed by junior nurses

explanation: It makes total sense: if sloppy or incorrect data goes into the computer, the resulting clinical alerts and reports will also be completely wrong. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h5)

question: What does data triangulation mean in community health assessment?

options.A: Interviewing exactly three family members per household
options.B: Comparing information from multiple sources to check for consistency
options.C: Dividing a survey questionnaire into three equal sections
options.D: Using three different brands of weighing scales for accuracy

explanation: You got it! Triangulation is simply cross-checking your survey results, interviews, and records to make sure your findings are solid.

question: What is the main goal of using the '5 Ps' framework when taking an adolescent's health history?

options.A: To calculate the exact body mass index of the patient
options.B: To determine the nutritional requirements of the teenager
options.C: To gather a thorough and structured sexual health history
options.D: To diagnose mental health disorders like depression

explanation: Spot on! The 5 Ps (Partners, Practices, Protection, Past history, Pregnancy prevention) help nurses collect sexual health details in an organized, non-judgmental way.

question: How does lacking formal education directly impact a girl's future health?

options.A: It guarantees that she will never contract chronic non-communicable diseases.
options.B: It automatically lowers her daily caloric and nutritional requirements.
options.C: It limits her access to health information, financial independence, and safe living conditions.
options.D: It protects her from experiencing workplace stress as an adult.

explanation: Education isn't just about passing exams—it gives women the tools to understand health messages, earn a living, and make wise choices for their families.

question: What is a major characteristic of passive immunity?

options.A: It stimulates the bone marrow to produce permanent memory cells.
options.B: It only occurs after a patient recovers from a severe viral illness.
options.C: It provides immediate protection that fades relatively quickly.
options.D: It requires the body several weeks to manufacture its own T-cells.

explanation: Passive immunity gives you ready-made antibodies right away, but it wears off because your body didn't make memory cells.

question: When should a nurse teach a client to apply cold packs rather than heat to an arthritic joint?

options.A: Right before starting a long walk or stretching routine
options.B: After physical activity when the joint feels swollen and inflamed
options.C: Only when the weather turns very cold outside
options.D: First thing in the morning when the joint feels stiff

explanation: Cold helps constrict blood vessels and numb acute swelling after use, whereas heat is better for relaxing stiff muscles beforehand. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h6)

question: What should you do if a patient calls reporting sudden chest pain and severe shortness of breath?

options.A: Ask them to send a text message if the pain gets worse tomorrow
options.B: Tell them to wait until next week for a routine clinic appointment
options.C: Instruct them to immediately seek emergency medical care or transport
options.D: Advise them to drink warm water and sleep for an hour

explanation: Safety first! Chest pain and severe breathing trouble are red flags. They need immediate physical medical attention, not home management.

question: Why must a triage nurse keep checking on patients who are sitting in the waiting area?

options.A: Doctors refuse to start treatment without fresh paperwork
options.B: A stable patient's condition can worsen while they wait
options.C: Patients get angry if their vital signs are not checked twice an hour
options.D: Hospital management requires nurses to update charts every five minutes

explanation: Illness can change fast! Someone who looked fine a few minutes ago can suddenly take a turn for the worse. Regular checks keep everyone safe.

question: Why should you avoid scrubbing a fresh needle-stick wound too hard?

options.A: It causes the wound to bleed much more than it is supposed to
options.B: It can cause skin abrasions and help pathogens enter the bloodstream faster
options.C: It ruins the shape of the skin and prevents proper medical documentation
options.D: It neutralizes the cleaning effect of the soap and water mixture

explanation: Be gentle with your skin. Vigorous scrubbing creates tiny micro-tears that actually help germs enter your bloodstream.

question: What natural biological feature in adolescent females makes them more vulnerable to certain sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Cervical ectopy
options.B: Enlarged ovarian follicles
options.C: Thickened endometrial lining
options.D: Hyperactive uterine peristalsis

explanation: You nailed it! Cervical ectopy exposes more delicate cells on the outer cervix, making young women biologically more susceptible to infections.

question: What is the main feature of a capital cost?

options.A: It involves a large investment in long-term assets
options.B: It changes every time a single patient is admitted
options.C: It covers minor daily items like cleaning supplies
options.D: It must be paid in cash at the end of every shift

explanation: Capital costs are big-ticket investments—like buying a new building or heavy machinery—that stay with the hospital for years.

question: What is a common resource barrier faced by nurses trying to maintain quality care in Nigeria?
